'''Yosef Hochberg''' ({{langx|he|יוסף הוכברג}}; 1945{{snd}}December 3, 2013)<ref>{{cite web |title=In Memoriam |url=https://en-exact-sciences.tau.ac.il/math/in-memoriam |website=en-exact-sciences.tau.ac.il |access-date=17 February 2025}}</ref> was an Israeli statistician and professor of statistics at [[Tel Aviv University]]. He is best known for the development (with [[Yoav Benjamini]]) of the [[false discovery rate]] (FDR) criterion and the [[False_discovery_rate#Benjamini–Hochberg_procedure|Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) procedure]] for controlling the FDR rate, as well as [[Family-wise_error_rate#Hochberg's_step-up_procedure|Hochberg's step-up procedure]] for controlling the [[family-wise error rate]]. 

Hochberg earned his PhD at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] in 1974.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hochberg |first1=Yosef |title=An Extension of the T-Method to General Unbalanced Models of Fixed Effects |url=https://repository.lib.ncsu.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/197bb240-2256-4600-904a-62b0cd93c8d3/content |publisher=North Carolina State University |access-date=17 February 2025}}</ref><ref name="bios">{{cite news |title=BiosRhythms |url=https://sph.unc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/112/2014/03/BiosRhythms2013.WEBversion.pdf |access-date=17 February 2025 |agency=Gillins School of Global Public Health |issue=25 |date=December 2013}}</ref> [[Pranab K. Sen]] was his doctoral advisor.

While on leave from Tel Aviv University, he visited the Statistics and Operations Research Department at [[New York University]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Conforti |first1=Michele |last2=Hochberg |first2=Yosef |title=Sequentially rejective pairwise testing procedures |journal=Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference |date=1 January 1987 |volume=17 |pages=193–208 |doi=10.1016/0378-3758(87)90112-1 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0378375887901121 |issn=0378-3758|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He became a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 1994.<ref>{{cite web |title=ASA Fellows |url=https://ww2.amstat.org/fellows/ |website=American Statistical Association |access-date=17 February 2025}}</ref> He was the seventh president of the Israeli Statistical Association.<ref name="bios"/>

He died on December 3, 2013.<ref name="bios"/> His daughter is Israeli-American scholar [[Gil Z. Hochberg]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=My Father, the Messiah: A Memoir |url=https://www.dukeupress.edu/my-father-the-messiah |access-date=2026-02-25 |website=www.dukeupress.edu |language=en}}</ref>
